About Hormuz Watch

A demonstration shipping-intelligence dashboard for the Strait of Hormuz.

What it is

Hormuz Watch is a demonstration dashboard that shows how a shipping-intelligence interface for a strategic maritime chokepoint can be built: vessel tracking views, shipping routes, oil price charts, war-risk insurance indicators, news feeds, incident timelines and regional impact assessments — all with explicit data-quality labels. It is a teaching and portfolio project: the architecture demonstrates a provider layer that gracefully degrades from live APIs to clearly-labelled demo data.

What it is not

It is not a real-time intelligence feed, a trading tool, a navigation aid, or a source of verified news. Vessel positions are fictional, price series are simulated, timeline incidents are invented scenarios, and insurance figures are illustrative estimates. Nothing here should inform commercial, navigational or safety-critical decisions.

Technology credits

  • Astro — static site generation and page routing
  • Svelte 5 — interactive islands and UI state
  • Tailwind CSS — utility-first styling
  • Leaflet — interactive vessel map
  • Chart.js — oil price charts
  • CARTO / OpenStreetMap — dark map basemap tiles
  • GDELT 2.1 — optional keyless live news API

Original branding note: this project's scope is inspired by the general idea of a public maritime-monitoring reference, but all branding, copy, scenarios and data on Hormuz Watch are original and created for demonstration purposes.

Disclaimer

All figures on this site are demonstration data unless a panel is explicitly marked LIVE. Do not use this site for trading, investment, navigation or safety-critical decisions. Headlines provided via third-party APIs are supplied as-is and are not verified reporting.
